context.exploration_scope: Connected both S21-ready Principles to the real SSI flow as independent, per-Principle change-gated triggers: compared each Principle's own last known real state against a fresh read, and ran a judgment loop only for the Principle(s) whose real state actually changed

problem: PHASE-SSI-S21 confirmed both Principles ready as a pair, but readiness alone does not connect either one to the real operational flow -- and wiring both in as a single combined trigger (rather than two independent ones) would risk running a Principle's judgment loop even when only the OTHER Principle's real state had actually changed, re-litigating settled state under the guise of the pair being "connected."

decision.decision_summary: P1 real_state_changed=false (left untouched). P2 real_state_changed=false (left untouched). 0 forced status changes. 0 CI wiring, 0 automatic policy, 0 automatic execution. Overall verdict: NO_REAL_TRIGGER.

action.action_summary: Compared each Principle's own last known real state (S21's fresh checkpoint plus the S5/S19 sub-field baselines) against a fresh read of the real trace/hold/overlay files; gated each Principle's judgment loop strictly on its OWN detected change; on change, computed the independent verdict before the Principle-guided verdict and compared them; never wrote to any real file.

evidence.evidence_detail: final_state=NO_REAL_TRIGGER, p1_real_state_changed=false, p2_real_state_changed=false, regression_all_passed=true, dangling=0, duplicates=0

result.note: Correctly reported NO_REAL_TRIGGER -- neither Principle's real state changed since S21, so neither judgment loop ran; both Principles stayed inert, which is the intended change-gated behavior, not a failure.

cause.root_cause_summary: Two Principles confirmed ready as a pair (S21) are still two separate real-world triggers -- a single shared change gate would either miss a real change specific to one Principle's own scope or spuriously re-run the other Principle's judgment loop for a change that was never actually within its scope; keeping the two change checks and the two judgment loops fully independent is what lets 'connected to the real flow' mean what it says for each Principle individually.

lesson: Generalizing a change-gated trigger from one Principle to two is not just running the same check twice -- each Principle needs its own last-known-state checkpoint (sourced from the specific prior phase that actually recorded it: S21's fresh trace read for chain_status, S5 for the gpu/hold baseline, S19 for the capability overlay/clarification baseline) and its own independent judgment loop, so that a change relevant to only one Principle correctly triggers only that one, and PRINCIPLE_REJECTED on one Principle never silently discards a valid PRINCIPLE_APPLICABLE result on the other.
